bullets: Own a revenue number. You're goaled on NDR against your book, with individual quota and individual accountability.

Sell after the sale. Identify expansion opportunities, build the case for increased budgets, drive adoption of new products and platforms as we launch them, and defend our share against incumbent agencies and channels competing for the same dollars.
Multi-thread across your accounts. Build relationships beyond your day-to-day contact, get to senior marketers and decision-makers, and know when to pull in leadership for top-down pressure.

Convert measurement into investment. Our clients validate creator spend through MMM, lift studies, and platform attribution that don't always agree. You'll navigate that landscape and sequence commercial asks around what a client's measurement will support.
Manage a full portfolio. Know where the growth is in your book, keep every account healthy, catch drift before the client tells you, and reactivate churned accounts.
Be the conduit between clients and product. You're the conduit between market and product. What you learn in client conversations steers what we build.

Real expansion wins you personally sourced and closed, at-risk accounts you saved, and budget you won before the performance data existed to justify it. Specific accounts, figures, and outcomes.

Deep fluency in ad platforms and performance data.
Comfort operating without a safety net. We’re a start-up that wants to move fast, we want someone that has the confidence to identify opportunities and the conviction to act quickly.

ashby:airgarage:5ca99583-725e-48af-8f88-.summary:
AirGarage is on a mission to bring real estate online, starting with parking.

We replace broken parking machines, fragmented software, and manual, labor-intensive operations with a unified, data-rich operating system for parking real estate. We handle everything it takes to run and optimize a parking asset: payments, dynamic pricing, enforcement, license plate recognition, analytics, and more.

By building all of our technology in-house, we are able to deliver a magical experience for drivers while providing real-time visibility and revenue increases of 20-50% or more for real estate owners. That’s why national real‑estate leaders like Hines and Greystar, as well as technology companies like Meta, partner with AirGarage to optimize their parking facilities.

sections.title: About AirGarage
paras: AirGarage uses datapoints like real-time occupancy, local events, weather, driver behavior, competitor pricing, and more to bring true intelligence to real estate owners’ assets for the first time.

We’re investing aggressively to make the physical world legible to a digital system: cameras, sensors, and software that generate a firehose of real-time data about the world around us. That data fuels models and algorithms that allow us to optimize performance at each property while giving owners the clarity and control they’ve never had before.
Before you can optimize an asset, you need to observe it. Before you can observe it, you need to bring it online.

Develop and execute detailed onboarding plans tailored to each property.

ashby:atticus:2bb334de-d501-4b02-bba6-8e.summary:
At any given time, 16 million Americans are experiencing a crisis that requires urgent help from our legal system or government. The right assistance could transform their lives. But today, most never get it.

Atticus makes it easy for any sick or injured American to get life-changing aid. Our mission is to tear down barriers between people in crisis and the aid they deserve. In the last six years, we’ve become the leading platform connecting people with disabilities to government benefits. We also help victims of accidents, misconduct, and violence get compensation from insurance.

So far, we’ve helped hundreds of thousands of people access over $10 billion in life-changing aid —and earned over 20,000 five-star reviews. And we’re just getting started.

sections.title: About Atticus
paras: We've raised more than $100 million from top VC firms like Forerunner, Google Ventures, and True Ventures, and we’re on our way to creating a category defining business assisting Americans in need.

sections.title: The Job
paras: In the next two years, we aim to help over 250,000 Americans get access to life-changing benefits. Much of that help reaches people through our Lawyer Network: our network of vetted partner law firms that represent clients alongside Atticus. The Lawyer Network (LN) team, led by Erin Casale , is the bridge between Atticus and those firms, and our job is to improve their ability to serve clients and help them grow.

We're hiring a Senior Account Manager to own our largest partner firms. You'll carry a deliberately small book of high-volume firms (roughly 10) and act as an extension of their team: diagnosing where and why they lose cases, coaching them on operations and legal execution, and getting even the most technophobic firm to adopt new Atticus tools.
The ideal candidate has spent years making small business customers measurably better at what they do through a mix of operations and tech, and wants to do that work somewhere it changes lives.
bullets: Make firms better. Own our enterprise-tier partner firms and improve their capacity, conversion rates, and win rates. Find best practices in firm operations and Social Security Disability legal execution, spread them across the network, and coach them relentlessly.

Drive technology adoption. Get every firm, including folks who are tech-hesitant, using new Atticus features well. That means making the case for the value (think: sales motion but the product is free), building and implementing change management plans, and running training and support.

Know your firms from the inside. Build relationships beyond the managing attorney, down to intake, case development, and operations leads. Understand a firm well enough to help with hiring, software, and staffing decisions, not just Atticus problems.
Be the voice of firms inside Atticus. Bring what you learn back to Product, Customer Experience, and Operations so we serve firms better and learn from their experience.

Deliver hard news well. Hold firms to clear performance standards and push back on attorneys—even those with decades of experience in the field—with finesse and confidence. If needed, cut ties gracefully.
Shape how the team works. Own strategic projects end to end, from scoping the question and gathering data to sharing recommendations with leadership and rolling out what works across the network.

sections.title: Who You Are
bullets: 5+ years in Account Management, Customer Success, Partnerships, or a similar role serving small businesses, where your mandate was improving your accounts' performance (not just retention)
A track record of driving product adoption in a tech or tech-adjacent setting
You read data comfortably, spot trends before results move, and show up with both a diagnosis and a plan
You're persuasive in conversation and in writing, and you'd rather pick up the phone (or get on a plane) than send another email

Adaptable: resourceful and steady when priorities shift

ashby:benchling:0796012f-3e8c-40b7-a869-.summary:
We are rebuilding biotech for the AI era.

When a breakthrough is delayed, the world waits. Getting a molecule from discovery to patients, or a crop from lab to field, involves thousands of slow, manual, disconnected steps. AI has the potential to change this, compressing decades of R&D work into years. But that only happens when clean, structured scientific data and AI are built into how science gets done.

Benchling is the AI platform for biotech R&D. Scientists use Benchling to design experiments, capture structured data, and run AI agents and models directly in their workflows. Over 200,000 scientists around the world trust Benchling to power their most important work, from academic labs to Sanofi, Moderna, and more than half of the world's top 50 biopharma.

We’re building an AI scientist for our customers. We can’t do that if we haven’t built the muscle ourselves. AI fluency is…

sections.title: ROLE OVERVIEW
paras: Schemas is the layer where our customers model their data. It’s a codeless configuration system powering all of Benchling's applications, representing a software abstraction around scientific data and processes. This system enables Benchling to ingest and store data at scale. You own the foundation that the rest of the product, and other Benchling teams, build on.

We’re looking for someone who owns the hard product calls and is the person customers, the field, and engineers come to for the answer, not someone who routes the question to engineering and waits for a reply. You’ll set the direction for the platform primitives, like computed fields, fieldsets, constraints, static properties, and data versioning, that speed up every team building on top of Schemas, and you’ll ship toward that direction incrementally while keeping the platform stable for the admins and developers who depend on it.

The integrated approach is what makes the Benchling platform different. Anything built in Schemas has to work for a wide range of customers and for the other teams building on it, so this role rewards a systems thinker who’s genuinely curious about the science and about how developers and admins actually use the product.

sections.title: RESPONSIBILITIES
bullets: Lead product management for our Schemas team.
Engage with customers, internal teams, and Benchling fields teams to understand their problems-to-solve and use cases.
Set the vision for Schemas that will help accelerate development amongst internal development teams.
Empower scientists, admins, and computational teams that use Benchling to turn their data into an AI-ready structured data foundation for the entire R&D lifecycle.

Comfortable with rapid prototyping, incremental shipping to deliver value to users, while also knowing the need to deliver stable features to our admins and developers. You ensure we ship well-crafted products at a timely pace.
Collaborate very closely with Engineering and Design to develop new product capabilities.
Partner with Customer Experience, Marketing, and Sales.

sections.title: QUALIFICATIONS
bullets: Ability to think in systems. Understanding what a customer wants and how that might impact various aspects of our product is essential.
Demonstrated ability to have a long term vision and ship incrementally along the way.
6+ years of product management experience
Experience with providing technical solutions to internal developers and external customers.
Demonstrated ability to explain technical concepts to customers and executive leadership.
Experience in B2B SaaS or Developer Platform industries preferred
Demonstrated experience setting direction and influencing stakeholders
A strong curiosity around the science processes that power the R&D lifecycle.

sections.title: The Role
paras: We're looking for a Customer Success Lead to own consumption across a book of Giga's enterprise production customers. Every enterprise contract we sign carries a minimum usage commitment. Your job is to get each customer to that commitment and past it: more conversations on the agent, more intents live, more channels and business units on Giga. You carry a number for it. You'll own each customer's timeline for getting there, and you'll push on it from both sides: externally, when the customer's team is slow to expand scope or route volume, and internally, when a product bug or a missing capability is what's holding them back. You sit between our Forward Deployed Engineers, who build and tune the agents, and our Enterprise Sales Representatives, who close the deals. You're the quarterback in the middle.

This is the first hire in a function we intend to build. You report to the CEO, you'll work directly with the founders and the revenue leadership team, and you'll define how customer success works at Giga before anyone else joins it.

This is not an FDE role and it's not a renewals desk. You won't be digging through tickets to find the root cause; the FDEs do that. You will know that something needs fixing, what it's costing the customer, and when it has to be done, and you'll drive it there. You'll also be the one telling customers what we're shipping and where the next use case is. When that turns into a real deal, the Enterprise Sales Representative comes back in to run it with you. You own usage and the timeline, they own paper.

sections.title: What You'll Work On
paras: As the first Customer Success hire at Giga, you'll be expected to build the playbook, not inherit one, and to show the CEO what the function should look like at 30 customers.
bullets: Consumption plans for every account in the book: Build the per-account plan from go-live to the annual minimum and beyond: which intents and channels go live in which month, what volume each one carries, and what has to be true on the customer's side and ours for each date to hold. Track it weekly and act when a week goes flat.

Escalations at the right altitude: When something breaks in production, you're the customer's single point of contact. You know what's broken and what it's costing them, you pull in the right FDE, you own the communication up to the customer's executive, and you stay on it until volume is back.

Executive cadence: Run monthly value reviews and quarterly business reviews with the customer's VP or SVP of Customer Care, Operations, or CX, with our CEO and founders in the room when it matters. The output is a bigger volume plan with dates on it, not a satisfaction score.
Making consumption visible: Work with RevOps to get usage against commit, and the blockers behind it, in front of the whole revenue org in Salesforce every week.

sections.title: How You'll Be Measured
paras: You own a defined book of production customers and you're paid on two things: every customer in it reaching full value on their commitment, and the book growing past it.

Compensation is $200,000 to $250,000 on-target earnings depending on experience, split 75% base and 25% variable, plus equity. Variable is paid quarterly, weighted 70% gross revenue retention and 30% net revenue retention across your book, with accelerators above target.

Here's how the number works. Every account in your book has an annual minimum commitment. We divide it into quarterly expected usage, adjusted for the ramp we agreed with the customer at signing, and those quarterly numbers add up to your book target. The GRR component pays on actual usage against that target and on renewals at or above commit. The NRR component pays on usage above commit and on expansion closed in your book, whether or not you sourced it. The Enterprise Sales Representative carries the quota credit on expansion; you earn the NRR credit when it lands.
bullets: Gross revenue retention. Every customer in your book consumes their full contracted commitment and renews at or above it. This is the floor, and it's most of the variable.

Net revenue retention. Usage above commit, new intents, new channels, new lines of business. You find it, quantify it with the customer, and hand a qualified opportunity to the Enterprise Sales Representative to close. They carry the quota credit, you get NRR credit when it lands.
Leading indicators we watch with you: time from production go-live to run-rate consumption, weekly usage against the ramp plan, and executive engagement on each account.

sections.title: What You'll Do
paras: A homebuilder's plan library is the product data behind its entire business, and at enterprise scale that data is almost entirely unstructured. Plans live as drawing sets scattered across semi-autonomous divisions, renamed and re-numbered as they move. Nobody can say with confidence which plans are duplicates, how many versions of a given home exist, or what actually varies between them.

Higharc converts those catalogs into structured, queryable plan data and builds the analysis on top of it: searchable plan libraries with agent-enabled natural-language search, geometric similarity scoring that surfaces plans which have forked under different names, structured mapping of what varies across a library, and classification that makes consolidation decisions possible.

You'll own what gets built in the field, working embedded alongside our Forward Deployed Engineers and in partnership with the homebuilder to turn plans into actionable data. This is a role for someone who wants to be close to where the problem lives. Higharc is fully remote; you can sit anywhere in the continental U.S., with travel to client sites and company events up to 30% of the time.
bullets: Embed with HQ, regional, and division teams to run discovery—locate plan assets, establish source of truth, and document how each division represents its plans and where variation originates.

Own product definition for the searchable plan library, analytics dashboard, and agent-enabled search—what a good query looks like, what a useful answer looks like, and what "structured for analysis" actually means.
Tune Higharc's Autotranslate AI to identify, categorize, and translate floorplans into data.

bullets: A suite of analytics and observability tools, including product analytics , replay vision , AI observability , and error tracking
PostHog MCP for users and their agents to query and act on their product and business data

Default alive . Revenue is growing incredibly quickly, and we're very efficient. We raise money to push ambition and grow faster, not to keep the lights on.
Well-funded. We've raised more than $180m from some of the world's top investors. We're set up for a long, ambitious journey.

sections.title: Things we care about
bullets: Transparency: Everyone can read about our roadmap, how we pay (or even let go of) people, our strategy, and how we work, in our public company handbook . Internally, we share revenue, notes and slides from board meetings, and fundraising plans, so everyone has the context they need to make good decisions.

Autonomy: We don’t tell anyone what to do. Everyone chooses what to work on next based on what's going to have the biggest impact on our customers, and what they find interesting and motivating to work on. Engineers lead product teams and make product decisions . Teams are flexible and easy to change when needed.

Shipping fast: Why not now? We want to build a lot of products; we can't do that shipping at a normal pace. We've built the company around small teams – autonomous, highly-efficient groups of cracked engineers who can outship much larger companies because they own their products end-to-end.

Time for building: Nothing gets shipped in a meeting. We're a natively remote company. We default to async communication – PRs > Issues > Slack. Tuesdays and Thursdays are meeting-free days , and we prioritize heads down building time over perfect coordination. This will be the most productive job you've ever had.

Being weird: Weird means redesigning an already world-class website for the 5th time. It means shipping literally every product that relates to customer data. It means building an objectively unnecessary developer toy with dubious shareholder value. Doing weird stuff is a competitive advantage. And it's fun.

sections.title: Who we’re looking for

sections.title: The Mission

Beyond implementing enterprise packages, you will define differentiated capabilities, validate them with working prototypes, and partner closely with Engineering to deliver production-grade applications. sections.title: AS A PRODUCT MANAGER AT SNOWFLAKE, YOU WILL:
bullets: Build Products from Zero to Production: Own discovery, vision, roadmap, prioritization, and delivery of in-house Order-to-Cash (O2C) products. Translate customer and operational needs into clear product requirements, MVPs, acceptance criteria, and measurable outcomes.

Own Contracts, Billing & Invoicing: Define capabilities for contract changes, order activation, usage rating, billing schedules, invoice generation, adjustments, and reconciliation. Support consumption-based, subscription, hybrid, and technical services business models.

Build Reliable Agentic Workflows: Define agent orchestration, tool integration, and approval checkpoints. Establish prompt and context strategies, evals, test harnesses, and observability to measure quality, reliability, latency, and cost.

Drive Adoption & Operational Excellence: Deliver measurable improvements in billing accuracy, automation, collections effectiveness, and adoption. Embed financial controls, security, audit trails, and resilient exception handling throughout the product lifecycle.

sections.title: Required Qualifications & Experience
bullets: Product Management Experience: 6+ years of product management experience building enterprise software, financial platforms, or billing products, with direct accountability for product decisions and business outcomes.

Deep Contracts, Billing & Invoicing Expertise: Hands-on product experience with contract lifecycle events, amendments, renewals, billing schedules, proration, invoicing, credit/debit memos, tax integrations, and reconciliation.

Consumption-Based Billing: Experience delivering usage-based billing capabilities, including usage ingestion and validation, metering and rating, tiered pricing, commitments, drawdowns, overages, and billing corrections.

End-to-End Quote-to-Cash (Q2C) / O2C Understanding: Strong understanding of the customer journey across CPQ, pricing, deal desk, contracts, orders, billing, payments, cash application, disputes, collections, and operational subledgers.

Core Software Product & Engineering Skills: Ability to translate business needs into functional specifications, data models, API contracts, workflow states, and testable acceptance criteria. Technical fluency in SQL, APIs, and event-driven systems, with sound judgment on build-versus-buy, scalability, and reliability tradeoffs.

sections.title: About the role

You will synthesize complex and fast-changing business needs and partner closely with the teams that retain, protect, and govern customer data across Anthropic's first-party platform and Claude on AWS, GCP, and Azure. Together, you will ensure that privacy guarantees are enforced by our systems and are verifiable by our customers.

This is a high-visibility role with substantial scope. Anthropic offers layered controls over how customer data is retained and accessed, and you will build the product surface that lets customers understand, govern, and verify these controls. This includes retention and access controls, access logs and compliance reporting, customer-managed keys and custody, data residency, and self-serve user interfaces. Your stewardship of these privacy capabilities earns the customer trust that is essential to Anthropic's mission.

sections.title: Key responsibilities
bullets: Deeply understand external customers with strict data handling requirements, from a bank's CISO to a healthcare system's compliance team to a government contractor's auditor, and the internal Trust and Safety, Legal, and GTM stakeholders whose needs pull in different directions.

Work with engineers to steer architecture and investment decisions with a long-term lens: balancing build versus buy versus rely-on-the-cloud-provider, and sequencing custody, residency, and transparency across clouds that ship on their own timelines.
Define success metrics for privacy controls, from preventing configuration incidents by design, to the speed at which customers can independently answer questions about their own data.

Define and iterate on the self-serve experience for compliance and security teams, expanding what an organization can check about its own posture, settings, and access history without having to wait on support tickets.

Gather and assess competing stakeholder needs and communicate prioritization trade-offs clearly to senior leadership, balancing privacy risk, safety requirements, legal exposure, and commercial impact. When something goes wrong, own what customers hear from us and when.
Work with engineering leads to decide how retention, access, residency, and custody controls are enforced, so that our infrastructure keeps the promises we make.

sections.title: The Opportunity:
paras: We’re looking for an enthusiastic, tech-forward product marketer to grow our Observability products by boldly positioning them and running campaigns to attract, convert and retain customers. As a Senior Product Marketing Manager, you will be in charge of the messaging and positioning for a broad product area. Then you’ll work closely with product managers and the marketing team to deliver campaigns, content, events, and training that help buyers buy (and sellers sell) our value.

Product Marketing lives within the Product org rather than the Marketing org at Grafana Labs, and we think differently about the job. Rather than purely executing launches or campaigns, we want PMMs to teach product managers and engineers in our org how to think about growth and demand, and to codify product marketing knowledge into AI-forward tools and processes that anyone in the organization can use. For example, we all contribute product information to a shared knowledge base, which we use to generate enablement materials and decks.

Grafana Labs is a fast-paced and growing organization. As such, this role requires strategic skills, an interest in teaching, and hands-on tactical execution (blogs, webinar outlines, video scripts, etc). Our team is full of people who crave impact and independence - if you are seeking a role with narrow scope where you run a defined playbook, this is not the job for you.

Conduct market and customer research to understand pain points, competition and opportunities.

Teach go-to-market and sales teams our products’ capabilities and the value they provide, deliver training and enablement, ensure customer facing teams are able to effectively engage with customers, partners, and prospects.

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

sections.title: About Gusto
paras: AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

sections.title: About the Role:
paras: The most senior individual-contributor seat in Solutions/Sales Engineering, not defined by a stage in the customer journey, but by scope: you're the final technical escalation point for Solutions Engineering, and the person who sets technical strategy and standard for the function as a whole. Where other Solutions Engineers own the deepest technical work on a given deal, you own the problems and decisions that span deals, route-to-market segments, and teams, like the ones with no existing playbook because nobody's had to solve them at this scale before. You're equally credible sketching an API flow with an engineer and discussing technical roadmap with an exec. In practice, that often means owning the deep API and OAuth-level integration and customization work behind the organization's highest-value enterprise and partner deals, the work that has historically had no clear owner, leaving sales and delivery teams to chase down the technical follow-through themselves.

sections.title: Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:
bullets: Serve as the final technical escalation point for the rarest, highest-ambiguity problems — the ones with no existing playbook.
Set standing technical strategy and direction for Solutions Engineering as a function, independent of any single route to market or deal.

Represent Solutions Engineering directly in cross-functional and executive conversations with Product, Engineering, and GTM leadership — translating technical reality into business decisions and vice versa.
Mentor and set the technical bar for the broader Solutions Engineering team — including coaching on the judgment calls that come with full deal/technical autonomy.

Own the technical strategy — and the hands-on build — behind the org's highest-stakes, most cross-functional initiatives: deep API and OAuth-based integration work for enterprise and partner accounts, from initial authorization through ongoing customization, end-to-end.

Act as the technical through-line between engineering/platform teams and go-to-market teams on the largest deals — making sure a committed integration or customization actually ships for the customer, instead of leaving that follow-through to sales.
Turn bespoke, one-off integration builds into reusable patterns and tooling other accounts and partners can adopt, rather than re-solving the same problem for every new deal.
Influence product and engineering roadmap from a position of pattern-recognition across the entire SE function, not just your own book.

sections.title: Here’s what we're looking for:
bullets: 8–12+ years of relevant experience, with significant time in a senior technical pre-sales, solutions-architecture, or implementation leadership role.
Proven track record operating independently on the most complex, highest-stakes technical problems an organization has — not just executing an established playbook.
Comfortable and credible in both a whiteboard session with engineers and a strategy conversation with executives — able to translate fluently between the two.
Demonstrated experience setting technical direction or standards across a team or function, not just for your own accounts.
Strong track record influencing product/engineering roadmap through structured technical feedback and pattern recognition across many accounts or problems.

Deep fluency across Gusto's technical surface area — Salesforce/CRM, API and integration architecture (including OAuth/token-based authorization flows), payroll/tax/compliance systems — sufficient to be the final word when others can't resolve something.

greenhouse:imbue:4452611009.summary:
Imbue is a radically different AI company.

We believe that data should belong to you, humans should come before technology, and everyone deserves to own a personal team of AI agents. We believe in a future of open agents that you can modify to do exactly what you want.

We’re building a suite of tools to make tech serve humans, and making it open source.

And we’re just getting started. If you’re excited about building a future with open agents, say hi!

sections.title: Summary
paras: We’re looking for a technical, people-oriented builder to help people get the most out of Imbue’s products, and help us build better products in return.

You’ll be one of the closest people at Imbue to our users. You’ll help them get started, understand what they’re trying to accomplish, troubleshoot problems alongside them, and discover where our products feel magical or fall short. You’ll bring what you learn directly back to product and engineering, helping shape what we build next.

You’ll also build the community around our products: creating spaces for people to learn from each other, share what they’re building, contribute ideas, and help shape the future of our products alongside us.

sections.title: What you'll do
paras: Your goal is simple: help people do cool things with our products, and make our products better because of them.
bullets: Work directly with users to get them set up, troubleshoot technical problems, and help them discover what they can do with our products.
Build deep relationships with our most engaged users and understand their goals, workflows, frustrations, and ideas.
Become an expert on our products and translate complicated technical concepts into useful, approachable guidance.
Create onboarding, documentation, examples, workshops, office hours, and other resources that help more people succeed.
Build and grow our user community, online and in person, and create reasons for people to learn, share, contribute, and come back.
Develop an unusually tight feedback loop between users and our product and engineering teams. Surface patterns, unexpected use cases, friction, and ideas that should influence what we build.
Find and tell great stories about what people are building with Imbue.
Build the systems and processes that allow us to support a much larger community as we grow.

sections.title: About you
bullets: You’ve worked in technical community, developer relations, technical customer success, solutions engineering, or another technical, user-facing role.
You’re technical enough to dig into how a product works, reproduce problems, troubleshoot with users, and communicate effectively with engineers.
You love talking to users and have a knack for getting past what someone asks for to understand what they actually need.
You can explain complicated technical ideas simply and clearly.
You’re good at building genuine relationships and communities, not just driving “engagement.”
You instinctively turn repeated problems into better documentation, tooling, product experiences, or processes.
You have strong product intuition and can distinguish an interesting anecdote from a pattern worth acting on.
You’re comfortable with ambiguity and excited to build something before there’s a playbook for how to do it.

This role is ideal for professionals with clinical and/or healthcare operations backgrounds and deep experience with health information systems who want to directly influence the evolution of enterprise EHR solutions used by healthcare organizations worldwide.

InterSystems EHR is a clinically focused, enterprise electronic health record platform supporting end-to-end patient care across hospitals and health systems. Data rarely sits still. It streams in through Kafka, flows through NiFi, gets transformed by Spark, and lands where Hive and Trino make it queryable at scale. When any part of that journey slows down or breaks, our customers' businesses feel it.

As a Product Specialist – Streaming & SQL Platforms, you'll be the expert who keeps that data moving for customers running Acceldata's Open Data Platform (ODP). You'll own complex escalations end to end, from ingestion and streaming through processing and SQL. You'll diagnose hard performance and stability problems, guide customers through migrations and upgrades, and make sure their mission-critical pipelines run reliably at enterprise scale.

sections.title: About the role
paras: This is a hands-on, customer-facing role for someone who thrives under pressure, enjoys finding root causes, and wants deep exposure to the platforms behind some of the world's largest data estates.

sections.title: What you'll do
bullets: Own L3 escalations across the data flow. Take complex issues in Kafka, NiFi, Spark, Hive, and Trino from first response to root cause and permanent fix.
Keep streams and ingestion healthy. Troubleshoot Kafka brokers, partitions, replication, and consumer lag, as well as NiFi flows, back-pressure, provenance, and cluster coordination.
Optimise processing and SQL performance. Analyse Spark jobs (executors, memory, shuffle, data skew) and tune Hive and Trino queries, plans, and resource usage for low latency and high throughput.
Lead migrations and upgrades to ODP. Plan for stability before cutover, support customers hands-on during the move, and tune performance afterwards.

Work across the full platform stack. This includes HDFS/Ozone storage, YARN and Kubernetes resource management, Kerberos and Ranger security, and Ambari-based operations in large on-prem environments.
Be the customer’s trusted technical voice. Lead troubleshooting calls during high-severity incidents, write clear RCAs, and bring recurring issues and product gaps back to Engineering.
Scale your expertise. Build runbooks, KB articles, and diagnostic playbooks that strengthen the wider support team.

sections.title: What you'll bring
bullets: 8+ years of hands-on experience supporting or operating distributed data platforms in production.
Deep expertise in at least two of Kafka, NiFi, Spark, and Hive/Trino, with working knowledge of the rest.
Strong Linux skills, JVM troubleshooting experience (GC, heap and thread dumps), and confidence with log analysis.

Practical experience with platform security, including Kerberos, Ranger, and TLS/SSL.
Scripting skills in Python, Bash, or Scala.
Calm, clear communication with customers during critical incidents.

sections.title: Nice-to-have

Contributions to Apache open-source projects.

lever:alertus:60745ad2-21b7-45dd-a88d-9c.summary:
At Alertus, protecting people from harm is our mission and our passion. As the leader in mass notification, we are committed to providing customizable, scalable, and cost-effective solutions, as we know even a few seconds of warning can help save lives during an emergency.

Our employees are integral to the company’s success and impact countless people's lives, safety, and well-being. We aim for a positive, collaborative environment that allows employees to work across departments easily and effectively.

sections.title: Job Description
paras: The Account Managers are responsible for working directly with our customers to ensure full, continuous satisfaction with our solutions and services are met. The Account Manager’s ultimate goals are to drive customer engagement and readiness of our solutions in times of crisis. Their engagement activities are responsible for building strong customer relationships that promote customer retention as well as ensuring customers are aware of opportunities to better complete their unified notification solutions with simple, easy-to-deploy automated crisis response tools they may not yet have.

The ideal candidate will possess strong communication and organizational skills. We're hiring a Technical Product Manager to own payments data products, both existing products and new ones built from zero to one. You will decide what we build, why it matters to customers, and how it works.

This role runs on an AI-native workflow. You will use AI throughout how you research, define, and specify products, and you own the quality of the result.

Jeeves is the stablecoin-native banking platform for global enterprises. Thousands of companies across 35 countries run their corporate cards, payments, treasury and spend on one platform, with more than $5B in annualized volume, payouts to 190 countries, and one of the fastest-growing stablecoin payment networks in the world. BMW, H&M, Lululemon, Burger King, Kavak and XP are among them, and more than 80% of customers use multiple Jeeves products.

We hire for one thing: relentlessness. A strong motor that keeps going when the problem has no playbook. You'll know in your first week if Jeeves is right for you. For the right people, it's the steepest learning curve of your career.

bullets: Onboarding: a fast, compliant application and KYB flow in every market we serve.
Underwriting: credit decisions, limits and limit increases, built with Risk & Credit to be fast, fair and explainable.
Activation: from approval to first transaction and first real value: card issuance, team invites, integrations and guided setup.
Spend management: controls, policies, budgets, approvals and AI-powered expense capture and coding for multi-entity, multi-currency companies.
Mobile: the Jeeves app for cardholders, approvers and admins, held to the quality bar of the best consumer apps.
Notifications: a reliable, configurable platform for real-time alerts across push, email, SMS and in-app.
Lifecycle communications: messaging that drives adoption, built with Marketing and Customer Success.
Analytics: customer-facing spend insights and reporting that finance leaders rely on every day.

sections.title: The Hard Problems:
bullets: Underwriting a company in Mexico, Brazil or Spain in minutes, when each market has different data, credit bureaus and rules.
Making spend controls for a multi-entity, multi-currency company feel as simple as a consumer app.
Extending the platform for large enterprises without losing the speed and simplicity other customers rely on.
Deciding where AI should act on its own (coding expenses, setting limits) and where a person must review, and proving it with evals.
Choosing which finance-team problems, customer segments and markets to take on next, and making the case for each.

bullets: 8+ years in product management, including 5+ years leading product teams and experience managing managers of PMs.
Product leadership experience building software products at a top-tier technology or fintech company (B2B fintech, payments or spend management is a plus).
Products shipped across multiple countries, currencies or regulatory environments.
Hands-on experience shipping AI-powered features to production, including how to measure whether they work.
Strong technical product depth in back-end, API and platform products, and an experiment-driven approach to owning metrics.
A deep understanding of how finance teams work day to day, and how to turn their workflows into great software.
Clear communication and strong partnerships with Engineering, Design, Risk, Compliance and go-to-market teams.

In this role, you’ll combine deep customer understanding, strategic thinking, technical fluency, and strong execution to translate business priorities into meaningful product improvements and innovations. You’ll partner closely with Engineering, Design, and business leaders to navigate complex decisions and drive initiatives from discovery through measurable results.

Your work will influence how GolfNow’s B2B products evolve, helping golf…

sections.title: Job Description
bullets: Own Product Outcomes: Develop deep expertise across GolfNow’s B2B products, customers, and business. Take end-to-end accountability for initiatives and measurable customer and business results.

Drive Product Strategy and Prioritization: Translate business objectives and customer insights into product priorities and roadmaps. Partner with Product leadership to shape direction, evaluate opportunities, and make informed tradeoffs.
Improve Customer Experience and Business Performance: Lead initiatives that simplify customer workflows, expand product capabilities, and drive adoption, retention, and revenue growth.
Accelerate Innovation: Identify emerging customer needs, evaluate new technologies and approaches, and lead the development of innovative product capabilities.

Lead Through Influence: Build strong partnerships across Engineering, Design, Data, Operations, Sales, and business teams. Communicate decisions and tradeoffs clearly while creating alignment across functions.

Deliver and Measure Results: Drive complex initiatives from discovery through launch and beyond. Define success measures, evaluate performance using qualitative and quantitative insights, and continuously improve products based on results.
